## Statement

Let $M_e$ be the positive definite electric mass matrix, let $S$ be the positive semidefinite conductivity matrix, and let $\Delta t>0$. Then $M_e+(\Delta t/2)S$ is symmetric positive definite, hence invertible. Thus each midpoint-conductivity Yee electric row has a unique solution.

2.1 A positive definite square matrix has trivial kernel: if $(M_e+(\Delta t/2)S)x=0$, then its quadratic form at $x$ is zero and step 1.1 forces $x=0$. A linear map from a finite-dimensional space to itself with trivial kernel is bijective, so the solve exists uniquely for every right-hand side. [step 1.1, algebra] ∎
cases.evidence: If the electric coordinate space has dimension zero, its unique endomorphism is bijective and the electric solve is the unique empty vector.

## Statement

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be any nonempty open set, let
$V=H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$, let
$K=\{u\in V:\operatorname{curl}u=0\}$, and put $X=V\cap K^\perp$ using
the $L^2$ inner product. Then $X$ is infinite-dimensional.

2.1 Each $v_j$ has compact support in $\Omega$, hence $v_j\in V$. For every $k\in K$, [F3] gives $(v_j,k)_{L^2}=\int_\Omega k\cdot\operatorname{curl}A_j\,dx=\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}k\cdot A_j\,dx=0$. Thus $v_j\in X$. Pairwise disjoint supports and $v_j\ne0$ imply linear independence: restricting any finite vanishing linear combination to $B_j$ forces its $j$th coefficient to be zero. The gauge space therefore contains infinitely many linearly independent vectors and is infinite-dimensional. [F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
cases.evidence: A single nondegenerate ball in the spatial domain already contains the explicit countable family of disjoint smaller balls used to prove infinite dimension.

## Statement

Let $A_j\in\mathbb R^{n_j\times n_j}$, $0\le j\le J$, be a finite SPD
Galerkin hierarchy with full-column-rank prolongations $P_j$ and

## Statement

Let $\Omega_i$ be one of the shape-regular polygonal subdomains in [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], with a matching quasiuniform $P_1$ mesh. For a continuous piecewise-linear boundary trace $g$, define

$$|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2:=\int_{\partial\Omega_i}\int_{\partial\Omega_i}\frac{|g(s)-g(t)|^2}{|s-t|^2}\,ds\,dt.$$

This seminorm is taken modulo constants. The local Schur energy satisfies

$$c\rho_i|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2\le g^TS_i g\le C\rho_i|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2,$$

where $c,C>0$ depend only on the fixed polygon shape, mesh shape-regularity and quasiuniformity. The upper bound is realized by a boundary-preserving finite-element lifting; the minimum-energy lifting is the discrete harmonic extension.

1.1 On the upper half-plane, Fourier transformation in the tangential variable gives, for a smooth lift $V$ with trace $g$, $$|\xi||\widehat g(\xi)|^2\le\int_0^\infty\bigl(|\partial_t\widehat V(\xi,t)|^2+|\xi|^2|\widehat V(\xi,t)|^2\bigr)\,dt.$$ Indeed, integrate $-\partial_t|\widehat V|^2$ and apply $2ab\le a^2+b^2$. Integration in $\xi$ proves the trace seminorm bound. Conversely, $\widehat V(\xi,t)=e^{-t|\xi|}\widehat g(\xi)$ has gradient energy $\int |\xi||\widehat g(\xi)|^2\,d\xi$. In a bounded chart, multiply the half-plane extension by a fixed cutoff in the inward coordinate; the added gradient term is controlled by the localized $L^2$ boundary norm, hence by the full H1/2 norm after constants are removed. A finite collection of Lipschitz graph charts covers the polygon boundary, including its corners. Flattening each chart is bi-Lipschitz, so it changes the $H^1$ gradient and boundary Gagliardo seminorm by bounded factors. Applying a partition of unity and the half-plane trace inequality to arbitrary chart-localized lifts gives $|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}\le C\|V\|_{H^1(\Omega_i)}$. Subtract the domain mean of $V$ and use scaled Poincar\'e to replace the full $H^1$ norm by $\|\nabla V\|_{L^2}$. In the other direction, apply a partition of unity to boundary data, use the half-plane extensions, and sum to obtain a right inverse of the trace. First subtract a boundary constant; the fractional Poincar\'e inequality on the connected polygon boundary controls the localized full norms by the seminorm. Add that constant back as a constant lift, which has zero gradient. The finite chart count and chart constants are uniform under [F1]. [given, F1, construct, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1/2<r\le1$, let $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)\cap H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ solve
$-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ distributionally, and let $h$ be the maximum
cell diameter of a finite matching shape-regular mesh. With the method of
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-poisson-method]], define
$$\mathcal R_h(u;v_h):=\widetilde a_h(u,v_h)-F_h(v_h),\qquad v_h\in V_h^{CR,0},$$
where $\widetilde a_h$ is the cellwise extension in [[def-crouzeix-raviart-poisson-method]]. Then
$$|\mathcal R_h(u;v_h)|\le C h^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(\Omega)} \|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
If also $1/2<s\le1$ and $\zeta\in H^1_0(\Omega)\cap H^{1+s}(\Omega)$,
then
$$|\mathcal R_h(u;I_h^{CR}\zeta)|\le C h^{r+s} |u|_{H^{1+r}(\Omega)}|\zeta|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}.$$
The constants depend only on $d$, the shape-regularity bound, $r$, and $s$.

2.1 Each jump in step 1.1 has zero face mean by [F2], so subtract the mean of its normal-gradient factor. Regard the finitely many facets as a disjoint union with surface measure on each component; Holder [F6] with the component functions $h_F^{1/2}(q_F-\operatorname{avg}_Fq_F)$ and $h_F^{-1/2}[v_h]_F$ gives $|\mathcal R_h(u;v_h)|\le \left(\sum_F h_F\|q_F-\operatorname{avg}_Fq_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2} \left(\sum_F h_F^{-1}\|[v_h]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2},$ where $q_F$ denotes the corresponding outward normal trace (and the boundary jump is $v_h$). By [F3], the first factor is at most $C h^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(\Omega)}$: each cell contributes at most $d+1$ facet terms, and the sum of the cell Gagliardo seminorms is bounded by the global seminorm because the integrands are nonnegative and $K\times K\subset\Omega\times\Omega$. The second factor is at most $C\|\nabla_hv_h\|_2$ by [F4]. This proves the general bound. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F6, step 1.1, given, algebra]

## Example

Assume Countable Choice. On the unit torus take the smooth autonomous velocity $b(x)=\sin(2\pi x)$ and any fixed time $T>0$. Its exact flow $\Phi=\Phi_{T,0}$ is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Use source and arrival cells $C_1=A_1=[0,1/4)$ and $C_2=A_2=[1/4,1)$ in a fundamental interval, with initial cell averages $(\rho_1^0,\rho_2^0)=(1,0)$. The flow fixes $0$ and $1/2$; on $(0,1/2)$ it moves points strictly to the right. Define $r:=\Phi^{-1}(1/4)$.

1.1 Since $b(x)>0$ on $(0,1/2)$, the forward trajectory from $1/4$ strictly increases and cannot reach the equilibrium $1/2$ at finite time by uniqueness in [F1]. Thus $\Phi(1/4)>1/4$, while $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi(1/2)=1/2$. Monotonicity in [F2] gives $0<r<1/4$. With representatives in the open fundamental interval $(0,1)$, $D_1=(0,r)$ and $D_2=[r,1)$, so $|D_1|=r$, $|D_2|=1-r$, and the nonzero overlaps with the occupied source cell $C_1\cap(0,1)$ are $|D_1\cap C_1|=r$ and $|D_2\cap C_1|=1/4-r$. [given, A1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

## Statement

Let $u_0$ be continuous and periodic, and use the explicit diagonal-diffusion
scheme of [[alg-na-explicit-diagonal-diffusion-hjb-grid-step]] with mesh
widths $h_{k,j}\to0$, time steps $\tau_k\to0$, and its diffusion-dominance
and CFL inequalities at every row. Then for every sequence of integers
$n_k\ge0$ with $t_k=n_k\tau_k\to0$ and $t_k$ within the computed horizon,
$$\sup_i|U_i^{n_k}-u_0(x_i)|\longrightarrow0.$$
The estimate is uniform over all finite control choices generated by the
maximization in the scheme.

2.1 Unroll $n_k$ updates as a finite transition tree. At a node of the tree, the maximum in the scheme chooses one of finitely many control rows; that row is a finite probability distribution by step 1.1. The terminal value is thus a maximum of finite weighted averages of $u_0(X_{n_k})$ plus accumulated rewards. On every branch the sum of the drift means has magnitude at most $Bt_k$. The centered increments have conditional weighted mean zero. For two different times, the weighted cross term vanishes by first summing the later centered increment over all branches extending a fixed earlier path prefix. Expanding the square and using step 1.1 gives, uniformly over all finite policies, $$\mathbb E|X_{n_k}-x_i|^2\le2B^2t_k^2+4dA_*t_k.$$ The accumulated reward has magnitude at most $Ft_k$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

Let $u_0$ be continuous and periodic, and use the explicit diagonal-diffusion

The estimate is uniform over all finite control choices generated by the
maximization in the scheme.

1.1 Fix one control row and abbreviate $\alpha=\alpha_j^a$, $b=b_j^a$, $h=h_j$. If $b\ge0$, the two neighbor transition weights in coordinate $j$ are $\tau(\alpha/h^2-b/h)$ at $x_i-h e_j$ and $\tau\alpha/h^2$ at $x_i+h e_j$. If $b<0$, they are $\tau\alpha/h^2$ at $x_i-h e_j$ and $\tau(\alpha/h^2-|b|/h)$ at $x_i+h e_j$. Their sum is $\tau(2\alpha/h^2-|b|/h)$ and their signed first moment is $\tau b$. The diffusion-dominance inequality in [F1] makes both neighbor coefficients nonnegative. The center coefficient is $1-\tau\sum_j(2\alpha_j^a/h_j^2-|b_j^a|/h_j)$, which is nonnegative by the CFL inequality in [F1]. Including the center, the row weights sum to one. Summing over coordinates gives mean displacement $\tau b^a(x_i,t_n)$. The raw squared displacement is at most $$\tau\sum_j\left(2\alpha_j^a(x_i,t_n)-|b_j^a(x_i,t_n)|h_j\right) \le2\tau dA_*.$$ Subtracting the squared mean cannot increase the second moment. [F1, F2, F4, given, algebra]

For a finite integer budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, the procedure

## Statement

Let $J\ge3$, $N=2^J$, and let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $1$-periodic and $C^2$, with $f|_U\in\mathcal S^2$ for an open interval $U\supset[0,1]$. Form the normalized sample vector $x_n=N^{-1/2}f(n/N)$ and its multilevel D4 coefficients $(a,d)$. For any $0<s<2$, set $p=(s+1/2)^{-1}$. Then
$$\|(a,d)\|_{b^s_{p,p}(J)}^p\le4M_0^p+\frac{(9\sqrt3M_2/2)^p\,2^{-2p(2-s)}}{1-2^{-p(2-s)}},$$
where $M_r=\sup_{[0,1]}|f^{(r)}|$, and for $1\le m\le N$,
$$\|x-U_N^TH_m(U_Nx)\|_2\le \sqrt{\frac p{2-p}}\left(4M_0^p+\frac{(9\sqrt3M_2/2)^p\,2^{-2p(2-s)}}{1-2^{-p(2-s)}}\right)^{1/p}m^{-s}.$$
The norm is the finite wavelet-coefficient convention of [[def-na-wavelet-coefficient-besov-quasinorm]]; no intrinsic Besov norm equivalence is asserted.

1.1 Here $1/p=s+1/2$, so the coefficient norm's scale weight is $1$ by [F4]. Orthogonality [F3] gives $\|x\|_2^2=N^{-1}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}|f(n/N)|^2\le M_0^2$, and therefore each of the four coarse coefficients has magnitude at most $M_0$. [given, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice only in the H(div)/Piola space branch inherited from the suppliers below. Let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh of a bounded polyhedron, with shape-regularity constant $\sigma$ and $h=\max_K h_K$. Assume material interfaces are mesh-aligned. Let $u,v$ be piecewise $C^1$ on cell closures, with $\operatorname{curl}u$, $\operatorname{div}v$ also piecewise $C^1$, and with matching tangential traces of $u$ and matching normal traces of $v$. The canonical edge and face moment interpolants $I_h^1,I_h^2$ are those in [[lem-na-whitney-moments-commute-with-grad-curl-div]]. Then
$$\begin{aligned} &\|u-I_h^1u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{curl}(u-I_h^1u)\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \quad+\|v-I_h^2v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{div}(v-I_h^2v)\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C_\sigma h |\Omega|^{1/2}\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\left(\|\nabla u\|_{L^\infty(K)}+\|\nabla\operatorname{curl}u\|_{L^\infty(K)}+\|\nabla v\|_{L^\infty(K)}+\|\nabla\operatorname{div}v\|_{L^\infty(K)}\right). \end{aligned}$$
The constant depends only on reference-element basis norms and $\sigma$. This estimate is only for the canonical smooth-input interpolants; it makes no boundedness claim on all of $H(\operatorname{curl})$ or $H(\operatorname{div})$.

3.1 Square and sum the four local bounds. By [F5], $h_K^5\le C_\sigma h^2|K|$; the cell interiors are disjoint and sum to $\Omega$. Taking square roots gives the displayed global estimate with the maximum cell derivative bound and the factor $|\Omega|^{1/2}$. The matching traces and the conformity part of [F3] assemble the interpolants globally. [F3, F5, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $U\in C^3([0,L],\mathcal G)$ have image in a compact subset of $\mathcal G$. On the uniform mesh in [[def-orthogonal-fv-compressible-viscous-scheme]], sample $U_i=U(x_i)$. For every interior face $x_{i+1/2}$, the defined viscous face flux satisfies

$$\left|G_{i+1/2}-K_{11}(U(x_{i+1/2}))\,\partial_xv(U(x_{i+1/2}))\right|\le C h^2,$$

for all sufficiently small $h$, where $C$ depends on $U$, the fixed physical parameters, and the compact positive-state set, but not on $i$ or $h$. This is a face-flux consistency estimate only; it asserts no mesh-uniform solution error bound.

1.1 Fix an interior face $x_f=x_{i+1/2}$ and put $U_f=U(x_f)$. Averaging the two expansions and using [F1] yields $U_{i+1/2}=U_f+O(h^2)$. [F1, given, algebra]

## Statement

Let $d=1$, $L=2\pi$, $a=1/2$, and let the probability measure $\mu$ have density
$$ d\mu(y)=\frac{1+a\cos y}{2\pi}\,dy. $$ For $\alpha_\varepsilon=e^{-\varepsilon/(2\pi)}$, the regularized neutralized source and zero-mean field are $$ \rho_\varepsilon(x)=\frac{a\alpha_\varepsilon}{2\pi}\cos x, \qquad E_\varepsilon(x)=-\phi_\varepsilon'(x)=\frac{a\alpha_\varepsilon}{2\pi}\sin x. $$ The gathered continuum target is $(\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon)(x)=\frac{a\alpha_\varepsilon^2}{2\pi}\sin x$. On any odd grid with spacing $h=2\pi/N$, the fixed-$\varepsilon$ theorem gives $$ \|G_hE_h-\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon\|_\infty \le (2\pi)^{1/2}h^{3/2}(\gamma_{N,2\pi}C_{\rm src}+C_3)+C_{\rm int}h^2, $$
where the constants are explicitly defined in [[thm-periodic-pic-smooth-density-grid-force-consistency]]. This tends to zero along odd $N\to\infty$ at fixed $\varepsilon$.

1.1 Since $0<a<1$, the density $(1+a\cos y)/(2\pi)$ is nonnegative and integrates to one. Convolving its constant and first Fourier modes with [F1] leaves the constant coefficient $1/(2\pi)$ and multiplies the cosine coefficient by $\alpha_\varepsilon$. Subtracting the neutralizing background gives the displayed source. Since $-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\cos x=\cos x$, the unique zero-mean potential is $\phi_\varepsilon=(a\alpha_\varepsilon/(2\pi))\cos x$, and differentiation yields the displayed $E_\varepsilon$. A second convolution multiplies its sine mode by $\alpha_\varepsilon$, giving $\eta_\varepsilon*E_\varepsilon=a\alpha_\varepsilon^2(2\pi)^{-1}\sin x$. [F1, given, algebra]

## Statement

Use the finite-dimensional realization and the hypotheses of [[alg-phase-field-convex-splitting-backward-euler]]. Assume $P_{c,h}$ is convex and coercive on $X_h$, and $P_{e,h}$ is differentiable and convex. For every $u^n$, $M>0$, and $\tau>0$, both branches have a unique minimizer. Their first-order conditions are exactly
$$\frac{u^{n+1}-u^n}{\tau}=-M\mu^{n+1}\quad\text{(Allen–Cahn)},$$
$$\frac{u^{n+1}-u^n}{\tau}=-M A_h\mu^{n+1}\quad\text{(Cahn–Hilliard)}.$$
The Cahn–Hilliard branch conserves $\langle u^n,\mathbf1\rangle_h$. With $\mathcal E_h$ as in the algorithm,
$$\mathcal E_h(u^{n+1})+M\tau\|\mu^{n+1}\|_h^2\le\mathcal E_h(u^n)\quad\text{(Allen–Cahn)},$$
$$\mathcal E_h(u^{n+1})+M\tau\langle A_h\mu^{n+1},\mu^{n+1}\rangle_h\le\mathcal E_h(u^n)\quad\text{(Cahn–Hilliard)}.$$
For the quartic split in [[def-phase-field-gradient-flow-and-double-well]], the required convexity and coercivity hold for both realizations.

2.2 The Cahn–Hilliard affine set is nonempty because it contains $u^n$. Its objective is continuous and coercive on that affine set by coercivity of $P_{c,h}$ and nonnegativity of the $A_h$ quadratic term. The inverse quadratic term is strictly positive on every nonzero mean-zero direction by [F2], so $J_{CH}$ is strictly convex on the affine set. The compact-sublevel argument of step 1.2 and [F3] therefore gives a unique minimizer. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, given, algebra]

The formulas in [F4] show that the remaining quadratic term in $P_{c,h}$ is nonnegative, so $P_{c,h}$ is coercive. The second directional derivatives of the two potential functionals are the corresponding weighted sum or integral of $F_c''(u)w^2$ and $F_e''(u)w^2$; [F4] makes them nonnegative, so both are convex. Thus both quartic realizations satisfy the coercivity and convexity assumptions. [F1, F3, F4, given, algebra]

## Statement

For every nonempty finite indexed dyadic planar site set, after duplicate collapse the algorithm of [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]] terminates. In the affine-dimension-two branch, after each insertion the augmented triangles are exactly the $d=2$ lower simplices of the common fixed-universe formal lift, as defined in [[lem-lower-lifted-facets-cover-the-convex-hull]]. After removing synthetic vertices, the output triangulates the input convex hull with weakly empty original circumdisks and coherent lexicographic ties. In dimensions zero and one, the algorithm returns the defined single site or consecutive chain.

1.2 In ordinary mode, `CHOOSE-SUPERTRIANGLE(P,0)` enumerates finitely many dyadic triples at each height and performs finitely many exact tests on each. [F1] guarantees an admissible candidate, so some finite height contains one and this search terminates; [F5] supplies terminating exact tests. The initial supertriangle is a triangulation and has no interior edge, so its edges are vacuously legal. Each input site lies strictly inside it by [F1]. The batch algorithm calls `INSERT(p,none)`, whose exact locator scans the finite current triangle list and tests each triangle with finitely many orientation predicates; [F5] makes every test terminate. Because the current triangles cover the supertriangle, the scan finds a containing face or an interior edge. Duplicate collapse excludes an existing vertex, and strict containment excludes a hull edge, so these are the only cases. An edge incidence lookup supplies the two faces of an interior edge. A supplied face or edge certificate is checked with the same exact predicates by the update procedure, without a scan; an invalid certificate returns its stated status. Splitting a face replaces it by three nondegenerate triangles covering it. Splitting an interior edge at its strict interior point replaces its two incident faces by four nondegenerate triangles covering their union. Both operations preserve a nonoverlapping triangulation. [given, F1, F5, A1, construct]

## Statement

For every nonempty finite indexed dyadic planar site set, after duplicate collapse the algorithm of [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]] terminates. In the affine-dimension-two branch, after each insertion the augmented triangles are exactly the $d=2$ lower simplices of the common fixed-universe formal lift, as defined in [[lem-lower-lifted-facets-cover-the-convex-hull]]. After removing synthetic vertices, the output triangulates the input convex hull with weakly empty original circumdisks and coherent lexicographic ties. In dimensions zero and one, the algorithm returns the defined single site or consecutive chain.

1.1 Consider any triangulation of a convex polygon whose interior edges all have the legal lifted incircle sign. The determinant identity [F2] is polynomial in the height entries, so it remains true coefficientwise for the formal heights [F3]; exact signs are supplied by [F5]. Across a shared edge the affine triangle planes agree on the edge. The legal sign says the opposite vertex of either triangle lies on or above the continuation of the other plane; the two tests are equivalent because the difference of the planes vanishes on the shared edge and changes sign across it. Thus the piecewise-affine height has nondecreasing slope when crossing the edge. For any triangle $\tau$ and any vertex $q$, choose $x$ in the interior of $\tau$ so $xq$ crosses edges transversely and avoids every other vertex; finitely many lines are forbidden. Along $xq$ the slope is nondecreasing, so the height at $q$ is at least the value of the plane through $\tau$ there. Every triangle plane therefore supports all lifted vertices from below; taking constant terms gives weakly empty original circumdisks. [F2, F3, F5, A1, choose, algebra]

## Statement

For admissible non-vacuum input data, the algorithm in
[[alg-safeguarded-euler-star-pressure-solver]] terminates after at most $N$
outer iterations and returns either a singleton exact root, a bracket
containing the unique $p_*$ from [[thm-euler-star-pressure-root-and-vacuum-criterion]],
or an explicit budget-exhausted status with that root still bracketed. After
$k$ completed non-exact iterations the bracket width is at most
$(3/4)^kP$. Thus any budget satisfying $(3/4)^N P\le\tau$ returns a
pressure-bracket status. No floating-point or nonlinear convergence guarantee
is asserted.

1.2 Assume the current bracket contains $p_*$ with nonpositive left and nonnegative right residuals. A midpoint query lies in its central half; any accepted Newton query is in the central quarter, and all other Newton outcomes use the midpoint. By strict increase in [F1], a negative query residual leaves the root to its right and a positive one to its left, so the corresponding endpoint replacement preserves the bracket; an exact zero returns the singleton. Every nonexact query is at least one quarter of the old width from either endpoint, so the new width is at most $3/4$ of the old width. [given, F1, F2, IH, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. On the spaces $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$ of [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]], equipped with $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_2$, the form $b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$ is bounded by $\sqrt d$. Its inf-sup constant satisfies
$$\inf_{q\ne0}\sup_{v\ne0}\frac{b(v,q)}{\|v\|_V\|q\|_2}\ge C_{\rm div}(D)^{-1}.$$

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. On the spaces $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$ of [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]], equipped with $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_2$, the form $b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$ is bounded by $\sqrt d$. Its inf-sup constant satisfies
$$\inf_{q\ne0}\sup_{v\ne0}\frac{b(v,q)}{\|v\|_V\|q\|_2}\ge C_{\rm div}(D)^{-1}.$$

2.1 For $q\ne0$, take $v=-B_Dq$. By [F1]–[F2], $b(v,q)=\|q\|_2^2$ and $\|v\|_V\le C_{\rm div}(D)\|q\|_2$. Thus $\sup_{v\ne0}b(v,q)/\|v\|_V\ge C_{\rm div}(D)^{-1}\|q\|_2$. Dividing by $\|q\|_2>0$ and taking the infimum over nonzero $q$ proves the bound. [A1, F1, F2, algebra, step 1.1] ∎

## Example

Take $A=I_2$ and the two coordinate subspaces. Exact local matrices are
$A_1=A_2=1$, so the exact preconditioner is $B=I_2$ and its condition number
is $1$. Choose inexact local matrices
$\widetilde A_1=4$ and $\widetilde A_2=1/2$. They satisfy
$\frac14 A_i\preceq\widetilde A_i\preceq4A_i$, while
$\widetilde B=\operatorname{diag}(1/4,2)$ and
$\kappa_A(\widetilde BA)=8$. The theorem's bound is
$(\beta/\alpha)C_0C_1=16$.

1.1 The coordinate decomposition is stable with $C_0=1$, and its synthesis bound is $C_1=1$ because $\|z_1e_1+z_2e_2\|_2^2=z_1^2+z_2^2$. Exact local matrices equal $1$, so [F2] gives $B=I_2$ and condition number $1$. [F2, given, algebra]

source_excerpts:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and use the separable Hilbert evolution triple $V=H^1(0,L)\Subset H=L^2(0,L)\hookrightarrow V^*$. Let $\Omega=(0,L)$, $T>0$, and use the conforming interval realization in [[def-phase-field-discrete-realizations]] with $h=L/N$ and time steps $\tau=T/J$, where $N,J\to\infty$. Fix $\varepsilon,\kappa,M>0$. For each $h,\tau$, initialize $u_h^0=P_hu_0$ with $u_0\in H^1(0,L)$ and use the corresponding convex-splitting scheme. Set $t_n=n\tau$ and, for $t\in(t_n,t_{n+1}]$, let $u_{h,\tau}(t)=u_h^{n+1}$, $\mu_{h,\tau}(t)=\mu_h^{n+1}$, and $D_\tau u_{h,\tau}(t)=(u_h^{n+1}-u_h^n)/\tau$; values at the finitely many endpoints do not affect the Bochner classes. There is a subsequence with $h,\tau\to0$ such that $u_{h,\tau}\to u$ strongly in $L^2((0,T)\times(0,L))$ and weakly in $L^2(0,T;H^1(0,L))$.

For the Allen–Cahn branch, the limit satisfies, for every $\phi\in C^1([0,T]\times[0,L])$ with $\phi(T,\cdot)=0$,
$$-\int_0^T\!\int_0^L u\,\partial_t\phi\,dxdt+M\kappa\int_0^T\!\int_0^L u_x\phi_x\,dxdt+M\int_0^T\!\int_0^L f_\varepsilon(u)\phi\,dxdt=\int_0^L u_0(x)\phi(0,x)\,dx.$$

For the Cahn–Hilliard branch, along a further subsequence $\mu_{h,\tau}\rightharpoonup\mu$ weakly in $L^2(0,T;H^1(0,L))$, and
$$-\int_0^T\!\int_0^L u\,\partial_t\phi\,dxdt+M\int_0^T\!\int_0^L \mu_x\phi_x\,dxdt=\int_0^L u_0(x)\phi(0,x)\,dx,$$
$$\int_0^L\mu\psi\,dx=\kappa\int_0^L u_x\psi_x\,dx+\int_0^L f_\varepsilon(u)\psi\,dx\qquad(\psi\in H^1(0,L)),$$
and $\int_0^L u(t,x)\,dx=\int_0^L u_0(x)\,dx$ for almost every $t$. The no-flux boundary conditions are encoded by the $H^1$ test spaces. The quartic nonlinearity is controlled here by the one-dimensional embedding $H^1(0,L)\hookrightarrow L^\infty(0,L)$. This theorem is for fixed $\varepsilon$ and $d=1$; it does not assert a higher-dimensional finite-volume limit or an $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ sharp-interface result.

5.1 Let $\phi\in C^1([0,T]\times[0,L])$ vanish at $T$. The sets $\{\phi(t):0\le t\le T\}$ and $\{\partial_t\phi(t):0\le t\le T\}$ are compact in $H^1$ and $L^2$, respectively, by continuity in those norms. Uniform operator bounds and strong convergence of $P_h$ in [F2] imply uniform projector convergence on each compact set: cover the set by finitely many balls of radius $\delta$, use convergence at their centers, and bound the errors inside each ball by the uniform operator norm plus $1$. Uniform continuity of $\partial_t\phi$ then shows the projected time difference quotients converge in $L^2$ to $\partial_t\phi$. Use $P_h\phi(t_{n+1})$ as the spatial test in the discrete equation [F9] and sum by parts in time. The terminal term vanishes exactly because $\phi(T)=0$; the initial term is $(P_hu_0,P_h\phi(t_1))=(u_0,P_h\phi(t_1))\to(u_0,\phi(0))$. Strong convergence of the tests, weak convergence of $u_{h,\tau}$ in $L^2(H^1)$ from step 3.1, and strong convergence of the nonlinear terms from step 4.1 permit passage in every sum, yielding the Allen–Cahn identity in the Statement. [F1, F2, F3, F9, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F:\widehat\Omega\to D$ be one admissible NURBS patch, $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, with determinant upper bound $j_+$, derivative and inverse-derivative bound $L$, and continuous denominator $W$ that is $C^1$ on each knot cell, satisfies $W\ge w_->0$, and has $\|\nabla W\|_{L^\infty}\le G_W$. Let $g\in C^1(\overline{\widehat\Omega})$ have Lipschitz gradient with constant $M_g$ and support contained in a nonempty compact set $K\Subset\widehat\Omega$, and set $\widehat u=g/W$ and $u=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$. On the uniform tensor grid of side $h=1/N$, use degree-one $C^0$ numerator splines and let $I_hg$ be the tensor Q1 nodal interpolant. If $h<\operatorname{dist}(K,\partial\widehat\Omega)/\sqrt d$, then $v_h=(I_hg/W)\circ F^{-1}$ is conforming in $H^1_0(D)$. If $u$ is the weak solution of an exact symmetric scalar elliptic problem with coefficient operator bound $\beta$ and coercivity bound $\alpha$ as in [[thm-isogeometric-poisson-galerkin-quasioptimality]], and $u_h$ its exact-form isogeometric Galerkin solution, then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{H^1_0(D),\nabla}\le\frac\beta\alpha\,C_F C_W C_d\,hM_g,$$
where $C_F=\sqrt{j_+}\sqrt{1+L^2}$, $C_W=2/w_-+G_W/w_-^2$, and $C_d=d+\sqrt d+2^{d-1}d\sqrt d$. These constants retain their map, weight, coefficient, and dimension dependence. This proves only the degree-one compact-support branch; it is not a general high-degree, knot-family, or locking-free rate.

1.1 If $g=0$, then $s=0$, $u=v_h=0$ and the result is immediate. Otherwise use the nonempty support set $K$ from the Statement. Every tensor cell meeting $\partial\widehat\Omega$ has all its vertices outside $K$: each vertex is within $\sqrt d\,h$ of a boundary point. Therefore $g$ is zero at those vertices, and the cellwise Q1 interpolant is identically zero on each such boundary cell. The function $s:=I_hg$ is continuous, has support in the compact $\sqrt d h$-neighborhood of $K$ inside $\widehat\Omega$, and is a degree-one tensor spline by [F1]. Both $s/W$ and $g/W$ are piecewise $C^1$, have matching traces because $s,g,W$ are continuous and $W\ge w_->0$, and have square-integrable cell gradients. By [F3] they belong to $H^1$; their supports are compact in the reference box, so [F2] puts them in $H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$. Pullback by [F5] gives $v_h,u\in H^1_0(D)$. [F1, F2, F3, F5, given, algebra]

## Statement

For a full-dimensional planar input in general position, augmented by a fixed supertriangle so the full set is also in general position, a uniform random permutation, the local insertion updates, and history DAG of [[alg-randomized-history-dag-point-location]] give expected $O(n\log n)$ total point-location work in the exact-predicate-call model. 1.1 Let $S_r$ be the unordered set of the first $r$ input sites, and let $p_r$ be the last site among them. Conditional on $S_r$, $p_r$ is uniform on $S_r$. The augmented triangulation has $m=r+3$ vertices and its fixed hull has $k=3$ sites, so [F3] gives $T_r=2r+1$ and $E_r=3r+3$. The degree of uniform $p_r$ is at most the average input-site degree, hence at most $(2E_r)/r=6+6/r\le12$. The number of final triangles incident to $p_r$ is its degree. During local legalization, the initial face split creates three triangles and each flip adds two triangles while increasing that degree by one; if the final degree is $d_r$, at most $2d_r-3$ triangle nodes are created in that stage. ## Definition

For left/right states in the neighborhood of
[[thm-local-small-data-riemann-solver]], let $u(\xi)$ be its self-similar
profile, $\xi=x/t$. If the profile is continuous at $\xi=0$, define the
**Godunov flux** by $G(u_L,u_R)=f(u(0))$. If it has a jump there, let
$u(0-)$ and $u(0+)$ be its one-sided traces and define
$$G(u_L,u_R)=f(u(0-))=f(u(0+)).$$
These fluxes agree by Rankine–Hugoniot at speed zero, so the definition does not
depend on the arbitrary point value assigned at the jump. This is a local
definition on the data neighborhood where the local solver is established.

For the midpoint-conductive update of [[alg-maxwell-yee-leapfrog-update]], define the same staggered cross-energy as in [[thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-energy]]. Then for every step
$$\mathcal E^{n+1}-\mathcal E^n=-\Delta t\left(\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)^Tj^{n+1/2}-\Delta t\left(\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)^TS\left(\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right).$$
With zero impressed current, this algebraic energy is nonincreasing because $S\succeq0$. Under the strict spectral CFL hypothesis of [[thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-energy]] it is also positive on admissible update states. Dissipation is asserted for this specified midpoint treatment, not for an arbitrary conductivity discretization.

3.1 If $j^{n+1/2}=0$, the balance and [F2] imply $\mathcal E^{n+1}\le\mathcal E^n$. When the strict CFL condition also holds, [F3] shows these nonnegative values control the admissible electric and centered magnetic state. [F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For the spaces and basis of [[def-signorini-dual-mortar-contact-pair]], put $d_i:=\sum_{e_k\ni a_i}h_k$. Then
$$\int_{\Gamma_C}\chi_i\phi_j\,ds=d_i\delta_{ij}\qquad(0\le i,j\le N).$$
The pair $(\Lambda_h,W_h)$ satisfies the mesh-independent trace-space inf-sup bound
$$\inf_{0\ne\lambda_h\in\Lambda_h}\sup_{0\ne g_h\in W_h}\frac{\int_{\Gamma_C}\lambda_hg_h\,ds}{\|\lambda_h\|_{L^2(\Gamma_C)}\|g_h\|_{L^2(\Gamma_C)}}\ge\frac1{\sqrt3}.$$
Moreover, $\lambda_h\in\Lambda_h^+$ defines a nonnegative functional on the cone of nonnegative functions in $W_h$, and $\langle\lambda_h,g_h\rangle=\sum_i d_i\lambda_i g_h(a_i)$.

1.1 On one edge, direct integration of [F1]–[F2] gives $\int_e\chi_L\phi_L=h_k$, $\int_e\chi_L\phi_R=0$, $\int_e\chi_R\phi_L=0$, and $\int_e\chi_R\phi_R=h_k$. Summing over edges, only the edges incident to node $a_i$ contribute to $\int\chi_i\phi_i$, and no edge contributes to $\int\chi_i\phi_j$ for $i\ne j$; hence the global pairing is $d_i\delta_{ij}$. This also proves linear independence of the $\chi_i$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, a shape-regular mesh with $h=\max_Kh_K$, and $I_h$ from [[def-na-rt0-h1-interpolation]]. There is $C$ depending only on dimension and the shape bound such that every $v\in H^1(D;\mathbb R^d)$ satisfies
$$\|I_hv\|_{L^2(D)}\le C(\|v\|_{L^2(D)}+h\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}),\qquad (\operatorname{div}I_hv)|_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K\operatorname{div}v.$$
If $v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, then $I_hv\in V_h$.

2.1 The divergence of $I_Kv\in\operatorname{RT}_0(K)$ is constant. For smooth-neighborhood approximants to $v|_K$ from [F5], Gauss–Green [F4] says the sum of their outward facet moments equals the integral of their divergence. The trace bound [F2] and H1 convergence let both sides pass to the limit, so $\int_K\operatorname{div}I_Kv=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}m_{K,F}(v)=\int_K\operatorname{div}v$. Dividing by $|K|$ gives the stated cell average. [A1, F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, a shape-regular mesh with $h=\max_Kh_K$, and $I_h$ from [[def-na-rt0-h1-interpolation]]. There is $C$ depending only on dimension and the shape bound such that every $v\in H^1(D;\mathbb R^d)$ satisfies
$$\|I_hv\|_{L^2(D)}\le C(\|v\|_{L^2(D)}+h\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}),\qquad (\operatorname{div}I_hv)|_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K\operatorname{div}v.$$
If $v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, then $I_hv\in V_h$.

1.1 Let $a_F$ be the vertex opposite facet $F$ in $K$ and define $\phi_{K,F}(x)=(x-a_F)/(d|K|)$. On $F$, $(x-a_F)\cdot n_K$ is the altitude $H_F$, so $\int_F\phi_{K,F}\cdot n_K=H_F|F|/(d|K|)=1$ by the simplex pyramid identity $d|K|=H_F|F|$. On any other facet, $a_F$ and $x$ lie in its hyperplane, hence $\phi_{K,F}\cdot n_K=0$. Thus $I_Kv=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}m_{K,F}(v)\phi_{K,F}$, where $m_{K,F}$ is the outward moment. By [F2], [F7], and Cauchy–Schwarz, $|m_{K,F}(v)|\le C(h_K^{(d-2)/2}\|v\|_K+h_K^{d/2}\|\nabla v\|_K)$. Also [F3] gives $\|\phi_{K,F}\|_K\le C h_K|K|^{-1/2}\le C h_K^{1-d/2}$. Multiplying and summing the fixed $d+1$ terms proves $\|I_Kv\|_K\le C(\|v\|_K+h_K\|\nabla v\|_K)$. Squaring and summing cells yields the global stability estimate since $h_K\le h$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F7, algebra]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the source-only Darcy system and hybrid equations of [[def-na-hybridized-rt0-darcy-system]] on a facet-connected mesh. The hybrid solutions modulo the common pressure shift $(p,\lambda)\mapsto(p+c,\lambda+c)$ are in one-to-one correspondence with the conforming RT0/P0 Darcy solution. If the mesh has at least two cells, every local flux-pressure saddle block is invertible; eliminating these local variables gives a linear system on the interior-facet multipliers whose nullspace is exactly the one-dimensional constant gauge. For one cell, the conforming flux and mean-zero pressure spaces are zero and the hybrid pressure is entirely gauge.

3.1 Invert the local blocks to express each $(u_K,p_K)$ as an affine function of the multiplier vector $\lambda$, with source-dependent right sides. Substitution into $J_F(u)=0$ gives a linear system solely on the finitely many interior-facet multipliers; this is static condensation. Existence and correspondence follow from steps 1.1–2.2. For its homogeneous nullspace, any multiplier vector yields a homogeneous hybrid solution, hence by step 2.1 a conforming solution with zero source. Uniqueness [F3] forces $u=0$ and $p_K=c$ for one global constant. The local equations then read $\sum_{F\subset\partial K,\ F\mathrm{interior}}(\lambda_F-c)\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K=0$ for all $v_K\in W_K$, since Gauss–Green and the zero physical-boundary flux give $D_Kv_K=\sum_{F\mathrm{interior}}\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K$. Using the independent facet basis [F5] gives $\lambda_F=c$ on every interior facet. Conversely a common constant vector is a null vector by the gauge identity in [F1]. Thus the kernel is exactly the constant gauge. [A1, F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.3, algebra]
cases.evidence: For zero source the conforming solution is zero, and every homogeneous hybrid solution differs only by the common constant pressure-multiplier shift.

The square finite-dimensional block is injective and hence invertible. [F5, F6, algebra]

Assume Countable Choice and the source-only Darcy system and hybrid equations of [[def-na-hybridized-rt0-darcy-system]] on a facet-connected mesh. The hybrid solutions modulo the common pressure shift $(p,\lambda)\mapsto(p+c,\lambda+c)$ are in one-to-one correspondence with the conforming RT0/P0 Darcy solution. If the mesh has at least two cells, every local flux-pressure saddle block is invertible; eliminating these local variables gives a linear system on the interior-facet multipliers whose nullspace is exactly the one-dimensional constant gauge. For one cell, the conforming flux and mean-zero pressure spaces are zero and the hybrid pressure is entirely gauge.

3.1 Invert the local blocks to express each $(u_K,p_K)$ as an affine function of the multiplier vector $\lambda$, with source-dependent right sides. Substitution into $J_F(u)=0$ gives a linear system solely on the finitely many interior-facet multipliers; this is static condensation. Existence and correspondence follow from steps 1.1–2.2. For its homogeneous nullspace, any multiplier vector yields a homogeneous hybrid solution, hence by step 2.1 a conforming solution with zero source. Uniqueness [F3] forces $u=0$ and $p_K=c$ for one global constant. The local equations then read $\sum_{F\subset\partial K,\ F\mathrm{interior}}(\lambda_F-c)\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K=0$ for all $v_K\in W_K$, since Gauss–Green and the zero physical-boundary flux give $D_Kv_K=\sum_{F\mathrm{interior}}\int_Fv_K\cdot n_K$. Using the independent facet basis [F5] gives $\lambda_F=c$ on every interior facet. Conversely a common constant vector is a null vector by the gauge identity in [F1]. Thus the kernel is exactly the constant gauge. [A1, F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.3, algebra]
